chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Jamarat (pillars of stone), so he said: 'Stand at the two Jamarat and do not stand at the Jamarat al-Aqabah.' I said: 'Is this from the Sunnah?' He said: 'Yes.' I said: 'What should I say when I pelt?' So he said: 'Exclaim Takbeer with each pebble.'

key_terms.السُّنَّةِ: The Sunnah, the prophetic tradition or established practice
key_terms.الْجَمْرَتَيْنِ: The two Jamarat (referring to the smaller and middle pillars)
key_terms.الْجِمَارِ: The Jamarat, the stone pillars in Mina used during Hajj
key_terms.جَمْرَةِ الْعَقَبَةِ: The Jamarat al-Aqabah, the largest and outermost pillar

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method and location for pelting the Jamarat during Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the specific ritual practice for the days of Tashreeq, distinguishing the pelting of the three Jamarat by noting that standing at the Jamarat al-Aqabah is not required during these days, a point of scholarly discussion regarding the continuity of the Sunnah. It further prescribes the verbal act of saying 'Allahu Akbar' with each pebble, emphasizing the mindfulness and spiritual declaration accompanying the physical act of stoning. This guidance reflects the Imami tradition's attention to the precise manner of performing Hajj rituals as transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt.
